x: The 2 miles run saw Jack Braughton, another 2nd claim member, turning out and from the virtual scratch mark he went through his field to win easily in good time.

Walker brought us to 5th on the third leg, and we then ran Jack Braughton in an endeavour to overhaul the leaders. Jack ran a fine lap in 14.7 which was only 5 seconds outside the course record set up by C.

We were not at full strength owing to the absence of Jack Braughton, Len Herbert, Archie Bedford and Len Adams, and did not expect to retain our team title, which we had held for the past two seasons.
Jim Masters was our first man home and deservedly gained his County Colours by finishing fourth. Our other scorers were J.

At this stage another second claim member, Jack Braughton, was just ahead of a large group of runners checked in at 29m.10s. which included Eric Gebbett, Len Adams, Ken Stimpson, Bert Jordan, and about another dozen runner.

As I have said the race started in perfect weather and at 3½ miles things had sorted themselves out with a leading group of 12, then Colin 14th and another group of 12 or so led by our second claim member Jack Braughton, with Eric 24th.

Walker, Jack Braughton, and Archie Bedford were among the non-starters and of those who were running only two were in full training. Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
J. Braughton, a second claim member was 6th.
Also taking part was Jack Braughton who has now become a first claim member. He will prove very valuable when he gets back to his normal form.

Several Belgravians can be found amongst the many photographs including Jack Braughton (2nd claim), Charlie Walker, John Bromley, Bill Nankeville, Peter Bagnall, Tom Morrell, Len Herbert, John Davies, Mike Shingles, Charlie Dabbs and Gerry North.

Other members of the British team had been Belgravians during the war including Doug Wilson, Rene Howell and Jack Braughton. Among the visiting teams Canada had a Belgravian as team manager but the Belgian marathon bronze medallist Etienne Gailly became one of the heroes of 1948.
